newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Guinea-Bissau civil servants suspend pay strike.
newsitem.headline: Guinea-Bissau civil servants suspend pay strike.

text.p: Guinea-Bissau's 12,000 civil servants returned to work on Thursday, suspending until next week a strike they started three days ago to demand higher pay.
"We have all started work today. But we are planning another strike for next Monday which will last for a week this time," union leader Desejado Lima Dacosta told Reuters by telephone.

The civil servants stopped work just three days after their country became a full member of the West African Monetary Union (UMOA) on August 1, and their currency, the peso, was abandoned for the Franc Zone's CFA franc.
Officials at the Dakar-based regional central bank, BCEAO, dismissed any link between the currency change and inflation, which is at the root of the campaign for higher pay.
"The strike has nothing to do with the replacement of the peso with the CFA franc," one central bank official said.
Authorities say they cannot consider raising salaries without the agreement of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund.
Union leaders say prices have shot up since the introduction of the CFA, making them Africa's lowest paid civil servants.
Many civil servants earn a monthly salary of just 10,000 CFA francs ($16). A bag of rice costs 11,000 CFA francs.
